alt: The string "Accra" with its characters at positions 0 to 4. LEN("Accra") is 5, so the last position is 4. POSITION("Accra", "r") is 3. SUBSTRING(1, 3, s) includes both ends and returns "ccr", while Python’s "Accra"[1:4] gives the same result by excluding the end.
caption: Positions start at 0, so the last character is at LEN(s) − 1.

alt: "New York" has 8 characters, because the space counts. In "banana", the letter a appears at positions 1, 3 and 5, but POSITION("banana", "a") returns 1, the first appearance.
caption: LEN counts every character; POSITION finds only the first match.

after: ## Processing a string one character at a time
alt: A FOR loop runs i from 0 to LEN(word) - 1 over "programming", taking one character each pass with SUBSTRING(i, i, word). The vowels o, a and i at positions 2, 5 and 8 are counted, so the output is 3.
caption: Loop over every position and take one character with SUBSTRING(i, i, s).

alt: In "Amara Diallo" the space is at position 5, so gap is 5. first is SUBSTRING(0, 4), giving "Amara", and last is SUBSTRING(6, 11), giving "Diallo"; the − 1 and + 1 leave out the space.
caption: Find the separator with POSITION, then cut either side of it with SUBSTRING.

alt: In ASCII, A to Z have codes 65 to 90, a to z have 97 to 122 and the digits 0 to 9 have 48 to 57. Because they run in sequence, adding 1 to the code of D gives E, adding 32 to the code of G gives g, and range tests on the code check for a capital letter or a digit.
caption: Codes run in sequence, so arithmetic on them moves through the alphabet.

alt: The cipher subtracts 65 to turn A to Z into 0 to 25, adds 3, wraps with MOD 26 and adds 65 back. Z (90) becomes 28, then 2, then 67, which is C; each O (79) becomes 17, then 82, which is R. "ZOO" is output as CRR.
caption: Subtract 65, shift, MOD 26 to wrap from Z to A, then add 65 back.

alt: The username takes SUBSTRING(0, 2) of "Okafor", which is "Oka", and SUBSTRING(2, 3) of the year converted to the string "2009", which is "09", joining them as "Oka09". Using INT_TO_STRING(year MOD 100) instead would give "9" and lose the leading zero.
caption: Convert the year to a string first, so the substring keeps the leading zero.
